title: Ambiguity around synchronicity for media resource selection algorithm

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
### ETA: I understood poorly before; Chrome and Firefox both update the `currentSrc` asynchronously, but only Firefox temporarily sets it first to the empty string

Original text:

I've noticed a discrepancy between Chrome and Firefox. When a `<source>` child of a media element in Chrome is called, and the `load()` method called, the `currentSrc` attribute is updated to the new value synchronously. However when the same is done in Firefox, `currentSrc` is *synchronously* updated to the empty string, then *asynchronously* updated to the new value.

Here's a jsfiddle demonstrating what I mean: https://jsfiddle.net/c60t1evn/10/

Now I looked into the spec and based on the [description of the load/resource selection algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#loading-the-media-resource) I'm not sure what the correct behavior is. I would appreciate some clarity.

Two things of note:
1. Step 4 of the resource selection algorithm, immediately before the synchronous section, says to [await a stable state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#await-a-stable-state). I'm not sure whether this means we should be waiting and letting the JavaScript call stack clear before *beginning* the synchronous section. If so, there would be a bug in Chrome. If not, I guess we might have a bug in Firefox.

2. The only place in the resource selection algorithm where `currentSrc` gets set to the empty string is in **object** mode - which suggests Firefox may be erroneously running in object mode instead of **children** mode (in which case this might be just a Firefox bug).
